instantiated_cells.justification: A "lobbyist" includes any individual who contracts for or receives "economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses," from a principal and whose duties include lobbying, with no dollar-amount compensation minimum stated.
The statutory definition of "lobbyist" is based on being employed/paid and (if not exclusively lobbying) on days of lobbying communications, not on the lobbyist's own lobbying expenditures.

The subchapter's reporting provision shown requires principals' expense statements and does not set any per-item de minimis threshold for itemizing individual expenditures on a lobbyist spending report.

A principal must register only after lobbying expenditures/obligations exceed $500 in a calendar year, and principals anticipating not exceeding $500 may file a verified statement and be exempt from licensing/registration/reporting requirements if true.

The statute provides a 5-days-per-reporting-period test to be a lobbyist (if not exclusively lobbying) and various principal-side reporting exclusions, but it does not create a lobbyist filing exemption keyed to a percentage of compensated time.
